The Industrial Revolution began in Britain in the late 18th century and transformed how goods were made. Hand production gave way to machines, and factories replaced cottage workshops. Steam power, first applied to pumping water out of mines, soon drove textile mills and later railways and ships. Cities grew rapidly as workers moved from farms to factories, often into crowded and unsanitary housing. Over time, rising productivity lifted living standards, but the early decades brought long hours, child labour and pollution that prompted the first labour laws and public health reforms.

Bees pollinate roughly one third of the crops humans eat, including apples, almonds and blueberries. In recent years beekeepers in many countries have reported colony losses well above historical averages. Researchers point to a combination of causes: the varroa mite, pesticides such as neonicotinoids, loss of wildflower habitat and climate-driven shifts in flowering times. No single factor explains the decline, which is why conservation programmes now combine habitat restoration, restrictions on certain pesticides and breeding of mite-resistant bees.

Context: Python's GIL (Global Interpreter Lock) is a mutex that allows only one thread to execute Python bytecode at a time in CPython. It simplifies memory management but prevents CPU-bound threads from running in parallel. I/O-bound programs are mostly unaffected because the lock is released while waiting on I/O. Multiprocessing sidesteps the GIL by using separate processes.

Summarise the following in 3 sentences, then give one sentence on the main trade-off.

Microservices split an application into small, independently deployable services, each owning its data and communicating over the network. Teams can release and scale services separately, and a failure in one service need not take down the whole system. The cost is operational complexity: distributed tracing, network latency, data consistency across services and a heavier deployment pipeline. A monolith is simpler to build, test and debug, which is why many teams start there and only extract services when scaling or team size demands it.
